definition: Tencent Hy, formerly known as Tencent Hunyuan, is a family of large language models developed by the Chinese technology company Tencent.
details: The Hy models are open-weight and use mixture of experts (MoE) architectures. The family includes Hy3 preview released in April 2026, Hy3 released in July 2026, and Hy4 preview released in August 2026. Hy4 preview has 770 billion total parameters, of which 49 billion are active for each token, and supports a context window of more than one million tokens. It is designed for tasks including software engineering, scientific research, financial analysis and the operation of AI agents.

explainer.lead: Tencent Hy is Tencent's open-weight family of large language models built on mixture-of-experts architectures. It matters because its largest release pairs 770 billion total parameters with only 49 billion active per token, making frontier-scale capability cheaper to run.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a huge company where only the few departments relevant to each request do the work. That is how Hy handles words: it holds enormous knowledge but only activates a small slice at a time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick Hy when they need open weights, long context, or agent and coding ability without paying for all parameters on every token. The pitfall is planning memory for the full 770 billion parameters even though only 49 billion are active per token.
tiers.paperLevel: A mixture-of-experts transformer: 770 billion total parameters, 49 billion active per token, context window over one million tokens. The known limits are the memory cost of storing all experts and the routing machinery needed to select them.

explainer.example: A financial-analysis pipeline loads Hy4 preview and feeds a document set exceeding a million tokens in one pass, with each token routed through roughly 49 billion active parameters instead of all 770 billion.
